subject: FinLytics: token economics & concurrency — post-demo next steps
messages:
From: Evan Cole <evan.cole@finlytics.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finlytics.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Feb 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Demo + econ conversation — quick clarifications

Thanks for the demo today, Jordan — good overview. A couple of quick clarifications on our end so we can validate the numbers with finance before we loop procurement:

1) Expected monthly token volume: current pilot shows ~120M prompt tokens + ~240M generation tokens (total ~360M tokens/month). We expect that to ramp to a steady-state band of 700M–1.2B total tokens/month over the next 6–9 months if POC metrics hold.

2) Typical request profile: ~60% short-chat (avg 60 tokens in, 120 tokens out), ~30% document-summarization (avg 1.5k in, 800 out), ~10% streaming inference for our note-capture feature (long-running sessions, ~5–10k tokens/session emitted gradually).

3) Concurrency characteristics: peak concurrent active users ~320 during business hours, but requests are bursty (top 5% windows see up to 900 QPS). Most traffic is steady during 9–6 PT; streaming sessions keep a long tail of active KV cache usage.

4) Budget band: Finance is comfortable with $5k–$20k/month initially; for production they want to target <$15k/month or clear unit economics at scale. They asked for a target $/1M tokens estimate for a realistic config (including batching and expected cache savings).

Can you send a short writeup with 1) $/1M token guidance for the profile above (pilot vs GA), 2) how continuous batching + KV caching would map to our streaming vs chat mix, and 3) recommended concurrency slab/instance counts for a predictable SLA? Procurement copied for visibility.

—Evan
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Evan Cole <evan.cole@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Feb 2026 17:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Demo + econ conversation — quick clarifications

Evan — great details, thanks. Putting the short writeup below and attaching a rough estimate + MAP (mutual action plan). High level summary first, then assumptions so you can pass to finance/procurement.

Summary estimates (ballpark, pilot vs GA)
- Pilot (no committed reserved capacity): $/1M tokens: $1,550 — assumes mixed model pricing, continuous batching active for chat/doc paths, streaming priced per-stream + per-token increment.
- GA (reserved + dedicated batching lanes, 12-month commitment): $/1M tokens: $680 — this reflects reserved slab discounts, better concurrency packing, and prefix/KV cache hit improvements.

Key assumptions and mapping to your profile:
- Workload mix: chat (60%), doc-summarization (30%), streaming (10%).
- Continuous batching: highly effective for chat & doc flows. For chat (short sequences), batching improves hardware utilization by ~2.2x in our runtime for your QPS profile; for doc requests (longer context) batching is limited by max sequence length but still yields ~1.4x token-level throughput.
- Streaming sessions: continuous batching less effective for per-token latency obligations; we recommend a dedicated streaming lane (lower batching, amortized per-stream overhead) with KV cache pinned per-session. Expect cache hit rates of 45–65% depending on repetition of context across the session.
- Concurrency mapping: with your peak burst characteristics, start with a 3-slab reserved footprint (N1 size) to cover typical day-to-day with autoscale headroom to 6 slabs at peak. That maps to sustained concurrency budget ~400–500 tokens-in-flight and spiky headroom to 900 QPS as you mentioned.

Operational levers to reach < $15k/month: 1) enable prefix/KV caching aggressively for chat and doc summarization, 2) adopt a small committed reserved tier (3–6 months) to capture slab discounts, 3) set per-route timeouts and early-exit heuristics for streaming tails.

Attachments: redwood_estimate_finlytics_v1.pdf (line-item per-route), FL-MAP-v1.xlsx (mutual action plan with milestones).

Next steps: 1) If these ballparks look reasonable, Marissa will prepare a formal SOW/quote and a reserved-capacity option. 2) Ben can run a short profiling test with a 24h synthetic workload (we'll need API keys and a small sample payload set). 3) If procurement needs legal/pricing terms, we can start a redline doc this week.

Happy to hop on a 30m follow-up tomorrow if helpful — available 10–12 PT.

—Jordan
From: Evan Cole <evan.cole@finlytics.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finlytics.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Feb 2026 08:41:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Demo + econ conversation — quick clarifications

Jordan — this is useful, thanks. A few quick clarifications from finance/prod after reviewing the numbers:

1) Pilot $/1M = $1,550 seems high for our pilot budget, but acceptable if we can show clear conversion to the GA $/1M. Can you provide the sensitivity (breakdown) that shows which levers move the cost most (batching, cache hit, reserved %)? A simple table would be great.

2) For streaming: our sessions are interactive but low-volume per account (many sessions with bursts). We care about percentiles (p95 latency) more than absolute throughput. Can the dedicated streaming lane guarantee p95 < 300ms for emitted tokens?

3) Procurement asked whether committed slabs can be phased (start with 3 slabs and ramp to 6 over 90 days) — please confirm price cadence for phased commitment.

If you can send a short sensitivity table + confirm p95 SLA feasibility for streaming lane and phased commit pricing, procurement will move to a formal PO review. We can shared a sample payload for Ben to run the profiling.

—Evan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Evan Cole <evan.cole@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Feb 2026 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Demo + econ conversation — quick clarifications

Evan — looping in next steps from our side. Attached is a 1-page sensitivity table plus a short SOW draft showing a phased commitment (3 -> 6 slabs over 90 days) with blended pricing tiers. Quick answers inline:

- Sensitivity: batching utilization and cache hit are the biggest levers; batching +/-10% utilization shifts $/1M by ~20–25% in your profile; cache hit +/-15pp shifts another ~10–12%. We'll send the exact table in the attached PDF.
- Streaming SLA: We can commit to p95 < 300ms for emitted tokens on the dedicated streaming lane with an SLA clause in the enterprise addendum, provided the model variant is one of the Redwood-verified low-latency models and traffic shaping is applied (we'll include fallback and prewarm guidance).
- Phased commitment: price cadence: initial 3-slab reserved pricing applied month 1–3; ramp discount applied month 4 onward after 6-slab average sustained usage. Doc includes explicit uplift schedule.

Action items: 1) Evan — please share sample payloads and a HubSpot record for procurement (we reference it in the DocuSign). 2) Ben — can you confirm estimated run time for the 24h profiling and a list of keys we need from FinLytics? 3) Jordan/Marissa — we'll prepare a clean SOW and send DocuSign for review by EOD Friday.

—Marissa
From: Evan Cole <evan.cole@finlytics.ai>

Thanks — I'll get the sample payloads and a PO contact over by EOD. The sensitivity table + SLA language will be the items our finance and legal teams focus on; appreciate the clarity.

One small ask: can Ben include a short note in the profiling run that captures the end-to-end latencies for the streaming lane at p50/p95/p99 so we can attach that to the procurement packet? That will help move the PO along.

—Evan
